issues.description: The function make_y_state has inconsistent parameter lists across artifacts. The problem statement declares the API as make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (depicted in problem_statement.md), and the reference implementation in solution_repository/msd.py implements def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. However, the template in template_repository/msd.py defines def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None (missing the depolarization probability parameter p). The template's docstring even refers to p despite the missing parameter. This inconsistency will confuse students and prevent them from implementing and using noisy |Y> state preparation (and will break downstream tasks that call make_y_state(circ, q, p)).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the depolarization probability parameter p to match the problem statement and reference solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update the template docstring to document the p parameter and ensure any internal comments or example usages in the template use the same signature.
